name_note: GTDB places Enterococcus faecium in the split genus Enterococcus_B; the organism is the same species that the literature calls Enterococcus faecium.

sentences.text: Enterococcus faecium is described as a commensal of the human gut microbiota that can become an opportunistic pathogen, particularly in immunocompromised individuals.
A review describes Enterococcus faecium as a commensal organism that has become a leading multidrug-resistant hospital-acquired pathogen, aided by genomic plasticity and horizontal gene transfer.
A meta-analysis of 349 studies estimated a pooled prevalence of vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium of 25%, and reported that this prevalence increased significantly over the last two decades.
A study reported that an Enterococcus faecium strain metabolised leucine to leucic acid and that colonisation with it improved obesity-associated metabolic phenotypes in obese mice.
